ai.description: *Cnemaspis limayei* reaches a snout-vent length of 35 mm. It is brown with a distinct yellow vertebral stripe and a dark lateral band. Key features include granular dorsal scales and a slender tail.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Cnemaspis limayei* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, continuous series of enlarged, spine-like tubercles along the flanks, which are absent in similar species.
ai.habitat: Cnemaspis limayei inhabits the rocky outcrops and boulders of the northern Western Ghats, typically found in moist deciduous forests at elevations around 600–800 meters.
ai.behavior: Cnemaspis limayei is a strictly nocturnal gecko that spends its nights foraging for small insects on vertical rock surfaces and tree trunks within its forest habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Cnemaspis limayei* is oviparous, laying a single, hard-shelled egg per clutch. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically from June to September.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Cnemaspis limayei* is endemic to the northern Western Ghats in Maharashtra, India, where it inhabits rocky outcrops at elevations between 600 and 1,200 meters.
